To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the feedback rate in MIMO broadcast channels with finite-rate feedback increases linearly with the SNR in decibels.

1) the throughput of the MIMO broadcast channel degrades as a function of SNR (in decibals) when finite-rate feedback is employed; 2) the feedback rate must increase linearly with SNR to avoid this degradation; 3) this is in sharp contrast with the point-to-point MIMO channel, where no such SNR dependency of the feedback rate is required; and 4) the throughput degradation is a function of the number of transmit antennas, but not

(a) in the downlink, the feedback rate per user must grow with the SNR in order to achieve full multiplexing gains, (b) the feedback rate required for a fixed multiplexing gain increases with the number of users, and (c) the feedback rate is not a limiting factor for downlink systems when there are a small number of users.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the capacity of multiple-input multiple-output broadcast channels with finite-rate feedback.
the design of a system that uses multiple transmit antennas in order to provide a large multiplexing gain to the downlink.
a fundamental tradeoff in the performance of MIMO broadcast systems with finite-rate feedback.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the downlink, the feedback rate required per user is linearly increasing with the SNR (in decibells) in order to maintain the full multiplex gains.
, for a given number of transmit antennas, the feedback rate must be increased linear in SNR in order to maintain the full multiplex gain in a downlink system.
the feedback rate requirement for a multiple-input single-output (MISO) channel is much more stringent than that for a single-input single-output (SISO) channel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the feedback rate must increase linearly with SNR to achieve the full MIMO multiplexing gain in a broadcast system with perfect channel state information at the receiver.
, the feedback rate per user must be increased linear with the SNR in order to achieve full multiplexing gains, while in a point-to-point MIMO channel it can be kept constant.
the capacity gain due to MIMO is not achieved in a practical system unless feedback rate is increased as a function of SNR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
feedback overhead is a critical design consideration in the downlink, but not in the uplink.
the feedback overhead in MIMO broadcast channels is significantly higher than in point-to-point MIMO channels.
the feedback requirement in the downlink MIMO channel grows with the number of users, and is proportional to the number of transmit antennas.
